notes:
- Built-in /security-review: the skill text was the genuine built-in. It ran against a tree where branch main equals origin/main with no commits ahead and an empty diff, so it covered nothing of the range ccb86f8..3f17ecb. I did the source-to-sink review by hand on the files in the Assignment. The tree is the holyagent-fix-cli-and-vcs worktree, read as it stood; I did not run any tests or commands.
- Result: no validated vulnerability and no suspicion strong enough to be a blocker. Nothing here was introduced or worsened by PR6 in a way an attacker could exploit.
- Non-blocking 1 (policy bypass, not a security boundary): hook commit-msg skips the phrase check on lines starting with the comment prefix and on everything below a scissors line (hook.ts lines 287-305). With `git commit -m` or `-F`, git's default cleanup keeps those lines, so `git commit -m $'x\n# the user asked'` keeps the forbidden phrase. Attribution trailers are still removed on every line, and `vcs commit` checks the whole text with no comment skip. Fix if wanted: run forbiddenPhrases on the whole cleaned text, or only skip comment lines when the cleanup mode strips them.
- Non-blocking 2 (comment contradicts code): generate.ts line 105 and hook.ts say the workflow hook runs onFailure: block 'because a failure would let an unvetted workflow through'. A failed non-blocking PreToolUse hook only falls back to the normal permission prompt, so block is not needed for safety. Its effect is that any crash or payload decode failure (exit 1) blocks the Workflow tool. This is an availability cost only. The two context hooks (subagent-start, vcs-reminder) and agent-launch are wired without block (dist hooks.json), so they cannot block.
- Non-blocking 3 (comment contradicts code): the originUrl doc in git.ts says the URL is 'checked for its host and slug', but repoSlug takes only owner/repo and checks no host. `gh api` then goes to gh's default host. A repo whose origin is on another host gets a PR request for the same owner/repo on GitHub, which fails unless the head branch exists there. No concrete exploit, so I did not report it as a vulnerability.
- Outside the named scope but in the diff: hook workflow (PreToolUse, permissionDecision allow) is the only hook that grants a permission. I only skimmed workflow-check.ts (closed AST node set, agent() literal agentType, denied reflective names, computed member keys only as integer literals) and saw no bypass. Earlier assignments reviewed it in depth.
evidence:
- Each finding is substantiated with a concrete input and the path it takes, or the report states none was found with the paths traced.: None found. Hook payloads: decoded by Schema.fromJsonString(Payload) (hook.ts 30-36, 67). subagent-start emits only the static bundled SPECIALIST_RULES, chosen by agent_type string prefix, with no payload text echoed, so nothing leaks and nothing is injected. vcs-reminder reads tool_input.command only to run the regex /git[\s\S]*(?:commit|push)/i and emits a constant string, with no permissionDecision, so it cannot allow, deny or exfiltrate. agent-launch: the id must match PROMPT_LINE (assignment-[a-z0-9-]+), agentId must match SAFE_ID /^[\w.:-]{1,80}$/ before it is echoed into a command, and recordLaunch only looks the id up in state (assignment.ts 110-128); no payload value becomes a path or command. hook commit-msg: the file path comes from git's argv; it reads the file and writes back only cleaned text (hook.ts 282-311); comment prefix comes from repo-file git config, not -c (160-167). vcs commit: Bun $ with array interpolation escapes each argument (process.ts 23-33), message goes through `git commit -m <headline>` as argument values, paths pass pathProblem (no absolute, '.', '..', ':' or backslash) and go after `--literal-pathspecs ... --` (git.ts 67-68, commit.ts 72-84, 104), staged paths outside scope are refused (commit.ts 100-102), and an agent identity is refused. vcs pr: the slug is regex-limited to [\w.-]+/[\w.-]+, branch passes validBranch (no leading - or +, check-ref-format), --update is /^[1-9]\d*$/ and apiPath-escaped, and the body goes to gh on stdin as JSON via `--input -` (github.ts 66-75). The body file is checked for project path, no .git segment, realpath containment, `git check-ignore --no-index` on the resolved path, O_NOFOLLOW open, size from the descriptor, and a re-resolve after the read (pr.ts 32-85). Tracing found no input that reaches a shell, an arbitrary path or the network beyond the intended gh call. See notes for the three non-blocking observations.
- findings: No validated vulnerabilities; no blockers. Suspicions are all non-blocking and listed in notes: commit-msg phrase-check bypass through comment-prefixed or post-scissors lines (policy only), the workflow hook's onFailure: block (availability only, and the rationale comment is wrong), and the missing host check in repoSlug (no exploit found). Hooks that block or leak: none for the two context hooks and agent-launch (no onFailure: block in /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent-fix-cli-and-vcs/packages/integrations/claude/dist/hooks/hooks.json); only the workflow hook can block, and only on its own failure.
